PullRequest.Title: Polish Customizations navigation and Extensions layout
PullRequest.Body:

The Customizations entry used a warning-colored migration indicator, while the Extensions section looked grouped with agent customizations and rendered an extra nested frame. This change aligns attention indicators with Automations, separates Extensions in navigation, simplifies the modal title, and lets Extensions use the shared customization panel layout.

- Uses the activity badge color for available customization migrations.
- Adds a divider before Extensions while preserving the existing extension-suggestion badge behavior.
- Changes the modal title from **Agent Customizations** to **Customizations** without changing the harness and workspace description.
- Removes duplicate Extensions page chrome so its title, padding, border, and content align with neighboring customization pages.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — Passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — Passed.
- Targeted ESLint for all changed TypeScript files — Passed.
- Targeted Stylelint for both changed CSS files — Passed.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\sessions\test\browser\sessionsList.test.ts --grep "includes the customization target|signals extension suggestions|switches the navigation treatment"` — 3 passing.
- Component Explorer render of 14 Before/After fixture and theme combinations — Passed.
- `git diff --check` — Passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Customizations editor, render its sidebar, and rebuild it after harness, configuration, count, or badge changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor synchronously enumerates the fixed management-section set, splices the visible rows, and renders each visible row. The diff adds one optional metadata read/copy and one classList.toggle per rendered row; no new asynchronous work must complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the persisted set of dismissed extension-suggestion badge IDs through IStorageService when the delayed singleton suggestion service is first instantiated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold read per service/window lifetime; warm editor opens reuse the singleton and derived observables.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same contribution already exposed getBadge, causing the same delayed service resolution and storage read before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This existing read can occur while resolving the Extensions badge on a cold editor open, but the new separator metadata neither introduces it nor changes its frequency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The sidebar is bounded by the 14 values in AICustomizationManagementSection, with effective cardinality reduced further by harness visibility and settings. Badge computation scans the cached installed-extension collection as before; the separator adds constant work per visible row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI/list-render pass. Rebuild triggers remain serialized on the UI thread, and the diff adds no queue, promise, listener, or concurrent work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Registry metadata is static. The extension-suggestion service is a delayed singleton, and its derived suggestion/badge observables cache until configuration, dismissal state, or the existing extensions-change signal invalidates them. The diff does not change keys, misses, invalidation, coalescing, or negative results.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: constructor, rebuild, renderer, registry, badge observable, and section cardinality were traced. The only added runtime operation is a constant-time class toggle per rendered section row.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact row count varies by harness and settings, but it is statically bounded and small; no realistic unbounded input controls the added class toggle.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added DOM class mutation participates in existing row rendering and is bounded to a small list; it does not add geometry reads, nested relayout, external calls, or materially more allocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Navigate to and use the Extensions customization section after the layout and separator changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: First navigation lazily creates the existing widget and synchronously groups the already-loaded local extension collection before painting its virtualized tree. The CSS removals and separator flag do not change widget creation, grouping, or I/O; later navigation reuses the widget.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist newly dismissed suggestion IDs through IStorageService when entering the Extensions section with undismissed suggestions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero writes when the dismissed set is unchanged; otherwise one write for the grouped set on navigation, not one write per extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Navigating to the section already dismissed and stored the current suggestion set before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing badge-dismissal write is reached from setVisible on navigation. The diff does not add the call, increase its cardinality, or move it onto a new path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Change extension workspace enablement, and optionally restart running extensions or reload the window, after explicit user actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One enablement operation per user toggle; one restart/reload operation per explicit runtime-action click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same user actions invoked the same enablement and runtime operations before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations are off the initial section-render path and occur only after explicit user interaction. The changed CSS and separator metadata do not alter them.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold rendering scales linearly with the cached local installed-extension collection; searching may perform the existing second grouping pass. The diff does not change extension cardinality, grouping, virtualization, or render frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Widget creation/render is one synchronous UI operation. Search remains coalesced by the existing 200 ms Delayer. Extension-change events schedule the same serialized render behavior as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The contributed widget is created lazily and retained in the editor's widget map for warm navigation. Installed extensions come from the existing in-memory workbench-service collection. Hidden renders remain deferred with renderPending. None of these cold/warm behaviors changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: lazy widget ownership, visibility transition, render path, search coalescing, storage dismissal, and enablement/runtime boundaries were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed-extension counts vary, but all collection-wide work is unchanged. The layout CSS may alter viewport dimensions slightly without changing the grouping or boundary-call mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR changes panel chrome and adds a visual divider, while preserving lazy creation, deferred hidden rendering, virtualized display, and all boundary-call counts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the Sessions list Customizations navigation indicator when migrations or extension suggestions change.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing derived observable chooses a filled-circle icon and the tree renderer consumes it. The diff only replaces one theme-color identifier with another; no additional work blocks rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per signal update, independent of session count; the changed branch already allocated the same icon object before the PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One existing observable recomputation on signal changes, serialized with the existing UI update path. No new listeners or asynchronous work are added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing derived observable retains its normal dependency-based memoization. The theme-token substitution does not change invalidation or caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete changed hunk and surrounding derived-observable definition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: the executed operation count and allocation shape are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; only the resolved theme token changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display the Customizations editor title in tabs or modal chrome.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: getName returns the localized title synchronously. The diff changes only the localization string literal.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per existing title request, with unchanged call frequency and string shape.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No scheduling or concurrency; the same getter calls occur as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Localization behavior is unchanged; no cache key or lifecycle changes are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the isolated getter change and its updated test.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; title computation frequency and cost are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and traced sidebar rendering, rebuild triggers, contributed-widget lifecycle, extension collection rendering, suggestion storage, and extension IPC actions. The PR adds bounded presentation metadata and CSS changes only; it introduces no actionable latency, throughput, CPU, memory, layout, I/O, cache, cleanup, or concurrency regression.
